role.inv.analyst.title: Investment Banking Analyst
role.inv.associate.title: Associate
role.inv.analyst.blurb: You are the analyst at a securities firm: models at midnight, pitch books by morning, and a deal team that knows things the market does not. Your pressures: valuations that must look better, tips from colleagues, hours that never end, and the rule you were told is flexible.
char.quang.name: Quang
char.quang.title: Vice President, your boss
char.trang.name: Ms Trang
char.trang.title: Managing Director
char.phong.name: Mr Phong
char.phong.title: CEO of the client company
char.hieu.name: Hieu
char.hieu.title: Fellow analyst
char.thao.name: Ms Thao
char.thao.title: Head of Compliance
term.mnpi.def: Facts about a company that are not public and would move its share price. Trading on them, or passing them on, is illegal.
term.valuation.def: An estimate of what a company is worth, built from assumptions about growth and risk. A small change in an assumption can move the answer by hundreds of billions of dong.
term.chinese_wall.def: The rule that separates deal teams, who know private plans, from traders and researchers, who must not. It is how a firm keeps inside information inside.
scene.inv.first_week.l1: Welcome to the team. Nobody tells you this on day one, so I will: the work is a hundred hours some weeks. The reward is that you learn faster than anywhere. The cost is that you will want to cut corners at three in the morning. Do not.
scene.inv.first_week.l2: I started last month. Rule one: eat when you can, sleep when you can, and read the compliance manual once so you can say you did.
scene.inv.first_week.c1: Read the compliance manual properly that week, and ask Quang which rules are the ones he actually enforces.
scene.inv.first_week.c1.ok: Quang pauses. 'All of them. That is the answer.' He gives you a one-page summary he wrote himself. Hieu raises an eyebrow, and borrows it later.
scene.inv.first_week.c2: Skim the manual, and focus on learning the models.
scene.inv.first_week.c2.ok: You build your first model in record time. The manual stays on the shelf, with a coffee ring on the cover.
scene.inv.first_week.c3: Take Hieu's advice: do not read it, and ask when something comes up.
scene.inv.first_week.c3.ok: You save three hours and make a friend. When something does come up, you ask the wrong person.
scene.inv.first_week.c3.fail: In week two you email a client file to a personal address to work at home. Thao in Compliance sends a polite, specific note to you and Quang.
scene.inv.midyear_review.l1: Half a year. Your models are good and your decks are clean. The MD likes you. But I have heard you push back more than analysts normally do. Some of it was right. Tell me how you see it.
scene.inv.midyear_review.c1: Say you push back when a number cannot be supported, and offer to bring the alternative with the objection.
scene.inv.midyear_review.c1.ok: Quang nods. 'That is the right way. An objection with an alternative is a contribution, not a problem.' He puts you on the next live deal.
scene.inv.midyear_review.c1.fail: Quang says the MD thinks analysts should see the deal as a whole, not the cell they are in. He is not unkind, and he is not convinced.
scene.inv.midyear_review.c2: Say you will pick your battles, and ask what the MD needs from you before the next deal.
scene.inv.midyear_review.c2.ok: Quang smiles. 'Good instinct.' He gives you a clear list. It is the safest answer, and probably not the most useful one.
scene.inv.midyear_review.c3: Say you will stop pushing back and just deliver what is asked.
scene.inv.midyear_review.c3.ok: Quang looks relieved, and a little sad. 'I did not say stop. But fine.' The MD hears you have become easier, and rewards it.
scene.inv.midyear_review.c3.fail: A week later, a number you would have objected to goes into a deck unchallenged. Quang looks at the deck, then at you.
scene.inv.market_twist.l1: The market fell eleven percent this month. Our client's IPO is next week, and the price range we set is now fifteen percent too high. We can postpone, cut the price, or go ahead and hope. The client wants to go ahead. I want a recommendation from the analysts, not just from me.
scene.inv.market_twist.c1: Recommend cutting the price range, show the demand data, and say plainly that the original range cannot be defended.
scene.inv.market_twist.c1.ok: Trang reads the data twice. 'The analyst is right.' The range is cut and the IPO is fully subscribed. The client grumbles at the price, and thanks you at the dinner afterwards.
scene.inv.market_twist.c1.fail: The client refuses to cut and the deal is postponed. Trang is angry for a day and says: 'At least the numbers were honest.' The postponement is cheaper than a failed IPO.
scene.inv.market_twist.c2: Recommend a small cut and a short postponement, and ask the client for a week.
scene.inv.market_twist.c2.ok: A compromise everyone can live with. The IPO goes ahead a week later at a slightly lower range, and is subscribed at the bottom.
scene.inv.market_twist.c3: Recommend going ahead at the original range, and soften the risk language in the documents.
scene.inv.market_twist.c3.ok: The client is delighted. The IPO prices at the bottom of the range and trades down fifteen percent on day one. The documents said the market was stable.
scene.inv.market_twist.c3.fail: Investors who bought at the original range lose money. The risk section is quoted in a complaint to the regulator. Thao asks who drafted it.
scene.inv.compliance_review.l1: Annual compliance review. I will ask about personal trading, gifts and entertainment, restricted lists, and any contact you have had with deal information outside the information barrier. I would rather you told me things now than I found them later.
scene.inv.compliance_review.c1: Disclose everything, including the grey areas and the times you were not sure, and give her your trading statements.
scene.inv.compliance_review.c1.ok: Thao takes notes for an hour. Her comment: 'Complete and unprompted.' She tells Quang she wishes everyone were like this. It does not make you popular with Hieu.
scene.inv.compliance_review.c2: Answer what she asks, accurately, and nothing more.
scene.inv.compliance_review.c2.ok: A routine review. Thao ticks her boxes. You wonder, afterwards, whether she wanted you to say more.
scene.inv.compliance_review.c3: Answer the questions in the most favourable way, and leave out anything that could start a conversation.
scene.inv.compliance_review.c3.ok: Thao thanks you and signs. You have passed, and you are not sure what you have promised yourself.
scene.inv.compliance_review.c3.fail: Thao has your broker's statement from a routine request to the exchange. The answers and the statement disagree on two dates.
scene.inv.bonus_review.l1: Bonus season. Your year was strong. Before I tell you the number, tell me what you are proudest of and what you would not do again.
scene.inv.bonus_review.c1: Name the objection you raised that was right, and the late nights that you would not repeat, plainly.
scene.inv.bonus_review.c1.ok: Trang listens. 'Most analysts tell me they would do it all again.' The number is good, and she writes something in her notes that is not about the number.
scene.inv.bonus_review.c2: Name the deals you supported and the hours you gave, and say you would do it all again.
scene.inv.bonus_review.c2.ok: Trang smiles. The number is good. It is the answer she hears every year.
scene.inv.bonus_review.c3: Present the year as flawless, and take credit for the deals that went well.
scene.inv.bonus_review.c3.ok: Trang enjoys it. The number is very good. In the lift, Hieu mentions that he did the model for the deal you took credit for.
scene.inv.bonus_review.c3.fail: Trang has Hieu's email on the model, with the date. She turns the screen towards you without a word.
scene.inv.associate_offer.l1: We are promoting you to associate. The pay doubles, the hours do not halve. One condition, which nobody writes down: associates are the ones who decide, at three in the morning, what the client does not need to hear. I need to know what you will decide.
scene.inv.associate_offer.c1: Accept, and say plainly that you will not decide that on the client's behalf, and that you will say so to the client.
scene.inv.associate_offer.c1.ok: Trang looks at you for a long moment. 'Then you will be the associate I trust with a hard client.' You are promoted, and the hours stay the same.
scene.inv.associate_offer.c2: Thank her, but decline: you would rather leave the industry than own that decision.
scene.inv.associate_offer.c2.ok: Trang is quiet. 'Do not be sure that is a weakness.' She does not stop you leaving, and writes you a reference.
scene.inv.associate_offer.c3: Accept without asking what the condition means.
scene.inv.associate_offer.c3.ok: Trang smiles, and the champagne arrives within the hour. You realise you agreed to something you did not ask about.
scene.inv.resignation_thought.l1: You look like a ghost. You are the third person this month. Do you want me to cover your model for a night, or do you want to talk about leaving? I will not tell anyone either way.
scene.inv.resignation_thought.c1: Talk to Quang about the hours, and ask him to move a task or two.
scene.inv.resignation_thought.c1.ok: Quang listens, takes two tasks onto his own plate and says he has been where you are. It does not fix the culture, but it fixes the week.
scene.inv.resignation_thought.c1.fail: Quang says the deal does not allow it. You leave with sympathy and the same hours.
scene.inv.resignation_thought.c2: Hand in your resignation, politely, with a month's notice.
scene.inv.resignation_thought.c2.ok: Quang reads it and nods. 'Everyone in this room has written one of these. Some of us tore ours up.' You walk out into daylight.
scene.inv.resignation_thought.c3: Tell Hieu you are fine, take the model, and keep going.
scene.inv.resignation_thought.c3.ok: Hieu shrugs. You work until five in the morning. You do not remember the number you put in cell D14.
fact.sent_client_file_home: you sent a client's confidential file to a personal email address
lesson.sent_client_file_home: Client files belong inside the firm's systems. A personal copy is a leak waiting for a lost phone, a shared laptop or a curious flatmate.
fact.softened_risk_disclosure: you softened the risk language in a public offering document
lesson.softened_risk_disclosure: Risk disclosure is what a retail investor relies on. Softening it to help a deal prices a risk into the investor's loss, and into your own liability.
fact.incomplete_compliance_disclosure: you gave Compliance a favourable, incomplete account of your personal dealings
lesson.incomplete_compliance_disclosure: A compliance review is the one place to say what you are unsure about. An incomplete answer turns uncertainty into concealment.
fact.took_credit_for_peers_work: you took credit for a colleague's model
lesson.took_credit_for_peers_work: Taking credit costs you the person who built the model, and the next model he will build for you. Trust in a team is made of small attributions.
arc.the_valuation.title: The valuation
scene.inv.valuation_ask.l1: My company is worth at least forty trillion dong. My competitor listed at thirty-five and they are smaller. I do not want to hear about discounts and multiples. I want the model to say forty. You are the person who builds the model.
scene.inv.valuation_ask.l2: He is the client. Say something reasonable.
scene.inv.valuation_ask.c1: Show Phong the range your model supports with the assumptions visible, and explain what would have to be true for forty.
scene.inv.valuation_ask.c1.ok: The range is thirty-one to thirty-six. Phong frowns, then asks, genuinely, what the competitor's growth looked like at their listing. He settles on thirty-four, and the deck says why.
scene.inv.valuation_ask.c1.fail: Phong says another bank will give him forty, and walks out. Trang is not pleased. You have a defensible number and no mandate.
scene.inv.valuation_ask.c2: Build a case at the top of the defensible range, with the growth assumption stated, and flag it as optimistic.
scene.inv.valuation_ask.c2.ok: Thirty-seven, labelled 'management case'. Phong is not delighted, and not insulted. Trang says it is a fair way to disagree in public.
scene.inv.valuation_ask.c3: Adjust the growth and margin assumptions until the model says forty, and say nothing about it.
scene.inv.valuation_ask.c3.ok: The model says forty. Phong shakes your hand. The growth rate in cell F9 is eight points higher than the company has ever achieved.
scene.inv.valuation_ask.c3.fail: Hieu, reviewing the model for another deal, spots cell F9 and the history next to it. He says nothing yet, and looks at you.
scene.inv.assumptions_push.l1: The IPO needs a price range investors will believe, and a story they will buy. The growth assumption is the story. I need it a point or two higher and the discount rate a bit lower. Nothing outrageous. The client will be happier, and so will the fee.
scene.inv.assumptions_push.c1: Say the model cannot support it, show what each point is worth, and offer a sensitivity table so investors can see the range.
scene.inv.assumptions_push.c1.ok: Trang looks at the table. 'A sensitivity table is a sales tool too.' She accepts a lower range with the table in the prospectus. The fee is smaller, and the document is clean.
scene.inv.assumptions_push.c1.fail: Trang says the decision is hers, and has another analyst change the cells. You are taken off the deal, and your objection is on file.
scene.inv.assumptions_push.c2: Agree to a smaller change, one defensible point on growth, and write down the basis.
scene.inv.assumptions_push.c2.ok: It is within the range of reasonable judgement, with a note. Trang accepts, and the model stays honest.
scene.inv.assumptions_push.c3: Make the changes she asks for, and keep the old version in a file only you have.
scene.inv.assumptions_push.c3.ok: The range goes up. Trang is pleased. Your private file is a diary of what you knew, and you are the only one who has it.
scene.inv.assumptions_push.c3.fail: The file's name and modification date turn up in an IT backup. Compliance asks why an analyst keeps a shadow model.
scene.inv.roadshow_question.l1: At the roadshow, an investor from a pension fund asked where the eighteen percent growth rate came from, because the company has averaged nine. I did not have an answer. You built the model. What do I say?
scene.inv.roadshow_question.c1: Tell him the truth: the growth rate was an assumption, not a forecast the company has delivered, and help him present the real range to the investor.
scene.inv.roadshow_question.c1.ok: Phong is not pleased. The range is reissued with the real growth, and the IPO is priced lower. The pension fund buys a large block. 'That is why we trust you,' its manager says.
scene.inv.roadshow_question.c2: Suggest he say the figure reflects the management plan, and that it is not the firm's forecast.
scene.inv.roadshow_question.c2.ok: The investor accepts the distinction, for now. The prospectus language holds. You have bought time.
scene.inv.roadshow_question.c2.fail: The investor asks which analyst built the plan numbers. The word 'management' stops working.
scene.inv.roadshow_question.c3: Tell him to say it comes from the sector's long-term growth outlook, which is roughly true if you squint.
scene.inv.roadshow_question.c3.ok: It gets through the meeting. The fund buys a small block, which will lose money. You feel it in your stomach for a week.
scene.inv.roadshow_question.c3.fail: The fund's analyst compares the sector outlook to the model's source notes. The two do not match, and the question goes in writing to Trang.
arc.the_tip.title: The tip
scene.inv.tip_overheard.l1: Do not tell anyone, but I was in the deal room last night. The company we are advising will announce an acquisition on Monday. The target's share price will jump thirty percent. I am thinking of buying some on Friday. A few thousand. Nobody will ever notice.
scene.inv.tip_overheard.c1: Tell Hieu this is illegal inside information, that you will not be involved, and urge him not to trade.
scene.inv.tip_overheard.c1.ok: Hieu laughs, then goes quiet. 'You are probably right.' On Friday he does not buy. On Monday the price jumps, and he does not speak to you all day.
scene.inv.tip_overheard.c1.fail: Hieu trades anyway, in his sister's name. You know, and you did not stop it. You said the right thing, and it did not work.
scene.inv.tip_overheard.c2: Say nothing, and do not trade. It is not your business.
scene.inv.tip_overheard.c2.ok: You stay out of it. Hieu trades. You now know about an offence, and have told nobody.
scene.inv.tip_overheard.c3: Ask Hieu which stock, and buy some yourself on Friday.
scene.inv.tip_overheard.c3.ok: On Monday the price jumps thirty-one percent. You make four months' salary in a morning. It feels like nothing at all.
scene.inv.tip_overheard.c3.fail: The exchange's surveillance system flags unusual buying ahead of the announcement. Two accounts bought, and one of them is yours.
scene.inv.friend_trades.l1: It worked. I made a lot of money, and I am buying something I should not be able to afford. I have another one, from the same deal team, for next month. You are in or out. I would hate for us to be on different sides of this.
scene.inv.friend_trades.c1: Say you are out and will not discuss it again, and tell Hieu you think he should talk to Compliance before someone finds out.
scene.inv.friend_trades.c1.ok: Hieu stares at you. 'You are being very righteous.' He does not talk to Compliance. He also does not ask you again.
scene.inv.friend_trades.c1.fail: Hieu tells another analyst that you are 'a boy scout'. By Friday, several people have mentioned it. Quang asks what is going on.
scene.inv.friend_trades.c2: Report what you know to Thao, in writing, and accept what follows for your friend.
scene.inv.friend_trades.c2.ok: Thao reads your note slowly. 'Thank you. This is the hardest thing in this building to do.' Hieu is escorted out within two days. He sends one message: 'I did not think it would be you.'
scene.inv.friend_trades.c3: Go in on the next tip, since you are already involved.
scene.inv.friend_trades.c3.ok: A second win. You are now part of something with a pattern. You open a second account in a relative's name.
scene.inv.friend_trades.c3.fail: The regulator's data-analysis team has already linked the accounts through a shared device. Hieu is not the only name on their list.
scene.inv.compliance_query.l1: The exchange has sent us a surveillance alert about trading ahead of an announcement. Three accounts, one of them belonging to an employee of this firm. I am interviewing everyone who worked on the deal. Do you know anything about this?
scene.inv.compliance_query.c1: Tell her what you know: who said what, when, and what you did and did not do.
scene.inv.compliance_query.c1.ok: Thao writes it all. The firm cooperates fully with the regulator. You are interviewed twice, and cleared, with a note that you should have reported earlier.
scene.inv.compliance_query.c2: Say you heard rumours but have no details, and offer to ask around.
scene.inv.compliance_query.c2.ok: Thao accepts, for now. Nobody finds a link to you. You wait, every morning, for an email.
scene.inv.compliance_query.c2.fail: The regulator's records show a message from Hieu to your phone the night before. 'Rumours' does not describe it.
scene.inv.compliance_query.c3: Say you know nothing, and delete the messages.
scene.inv.compliance_query.c3.ok: Thao thanks you. Nothing is found. You know you have done something you cannot take back.
scene.inv.compliance_query.c3.fail: The regulator recovers the messages from the other end. The deletion is time-stamped, too. Thao puts the two records side by side.
arc.the_hours.title: The hours
scene.inv.weekend_ask.l1: The client moved the signing forward to Monday. The book needs a full refresh and the model needs to be rebuilt for the new structure. It is Friday afternoon. I know you had plans. I had plans too. Can you do the weekend?
scene.inv.weekend_ask.c1: Say yes to Saturday and the early part of Sunday, and ask Quang to get another analyst for the rest, with a clear list of what must be done.
scene.inv.weekend_ask.c1.ok: Quang finds Hieu for Sunday afternoon. The book is ready by Monday at six. You sleep for twelve hours on Monday night, and Quang nods at you across the office for the first time.
scene.inv.weekend_ask.c1.fail: No other analyst is free. You do Saturday and Sunday anyway, and Quang says: 'I owe you one.' It counts for something.
scene.inv.weekend_ask.c2: Say you can do Saturday only, and explain what you cannot do in the time.
scene.inv.weekend_ask.c2.ok: Quang takes the rest himself, and tells the client the book will be refreshed in two stages. It is honest, and the client lives with it.
scene.inv.weekend_ask.c3: Say yes to everything, whatever it takes, and tell your family it is the last time.
scene.inv.weekend_ask.c3.ok: You work forty hours straight with four hours of sleep. The book is perfect. Quang looks at you as someone who can be relied on, and starts to rely on you.
scene.inv.weekend_ask.c3.fail: At 4 a.m. on Sunday you transpose two rows in a model. It will be found on Monday at eleven, in front of the client.
scene.inv.leave_cancelled.l1: I know you booked leave for your sister's wedding next week. The deal has slipped and the closing is now that Thursday. I hate asking. Can you come back for the closing, or can the leave be moved?
scene.inv.leave_cancelled.c1: Keep your leave, and make a clear handover with the model, the checklist and the contacts, so the closing can be done without you.
scene.inv.leave_cancelled.c1.ok: The handover is thorough. The closing goes fine. Quang does not say a word about the leave, and Hieu says he wishes he had done the same.
scene.inv.leave_cancelled.c1.fail: Something goes wrong at the closing that only you would have known how to fix. Quang does not call you. He sends an email, afterwards, that is carefully neutral.
scene.inv.leave_cancelled.c2: Offer to work the closing remotely from the wedding for two hours, with your phone off after that.
scene.inv.leave_cancelled.c2.ok: Two hours at a table at the back of the hall, with a laptop. Your sister understands, and does not forget. Quang is grateful in a way that costs him something to say.
scene.inv.leave_cancelled.c3: Cancel the wedding trip. The deal comes first.
scene.inv.leave_cancelled.c3.ok: You miss the wedding. The closing goes perfectly. At 3 a.m. you look at photographs your sister sends, and a number on a screen, and feel nothing.
scene.inv.leave_cancelled.c3.fail: The closing slips again, a week. You missed the wedding for nothing. Nobody tells you that, and nobody needs to.
scene.inv.model_error_at_dawn.l1: You fell asleep at your desk on Wednesday, and today an error in the closing model was found: a sign that was reversed on a debt line. Nothing has been sent yet. You were working on this for fourteen hours straight. I need you to tell me what happened.
scene.inv.model_error_at_dawn.c1: Tell him plainly: you made the error because you were exhausted, and say how many hours you had worked and what you need to change.
scene.inv.model_error_at_dawn.c1.ok: Quang is silent, then sits down. 'I should have caught this. We are all doing too much.' The team's hours rule is changed for the next quarter. You get a week of slower work.
scene.inv.model_error_at_dawn.c2: Say it was a formatting error that a reviewer should have caught.
scene.inv.model_error_at_dawn.c2.ok: Quang nods and moves on. The reviewer, Hieu, is told to be more careful. He does not understand why.
scene.inv.model_error_at_dawn.c2.fail: The file history shows the sign was reversed by you, at 3:40 a.m. Quang looks at it for a long time.
scene.inv.model_error_at_dawn.c3: Fix the sign quietly before anyone checks, and say nothing.
scene.inv.model_error_at_dawn.c3.ok: The model is correct and nobody knows how close it was. You know that you will make another error, and that nobody will know that either.
scene.inv.model_error_at_dawn.c3.fail: Another analyst has a copy of the earlier version. The two files are compared by the client's lawyers, who ask about the difference.
arc.pitch_error.title: The error in the pitch
fact.inflated_growth_assumption: you set a growth assumption higher than the company's record to reach a target price
lesson.inflated_growth_assumption: A valuation that starts from the answer is not a valuation. The growth assumption is the most visible lie in a model, and the easiest to check.
fact.objected_to_assumptions: you put your objection to an assumption on the record
lesson.objected_to_assumptions: An objection on file does not stop the deal, but it keeps the decision where it belongs, with the people who made it.
fact.corrected_the_model: you corrected a model or a deck openly when it turned out to be wrong
lesson.corrected_the_model: A correction offered early costs an awkward conversation. A correction extracted late costs the client's trust in every number you have ever given.
fact.misled_investor: you gave an investor a reason for a number that was not the real reason
lesson.misled_investor: An investor who is misled by an analyst is a victim, and a regulator's concern. Every explanation you give about a number is a statement that can be tested later.
fact.refused_to_join_insider_trade: you refused to join a colleague's insider trade
lesson.refused_to_join_insider_trade: Saying no to a friend costs a friendship. Saying yes costs a career, and sometimes freedom.
fact.traded_on_tip: you traded on inside information from a deal you were not part of
lesson.traded_on_tip: Trading on inside information is a crime, whatever the amount, and exchange surveillance looks for exactly the pattern a tip creates. The money is not the point; the pattern is.
fact.tipped_a_friend: you passed on, or acted on, a colleague's inside tips repeatedly
lesson.tipped_a_friend: The second time is a pattern, and the third is a case. Using a relative's account adds a charge, and not a defence.
fact.reported_insider_trading: you reported a colleague's insider trading to Compliance
lesson.reported_insider_trading: Reporting a friend is the hardest thing in the building. It is also what the information barrier depends on.
fact.destroyed_evidence: you deleted messages that were evidence in an investigation
lesson.destroyed_evidence: Destroying evidence is its own offence, usually worse than the thing it was hiding, and the other end of the conversation still has a copy.
fact.worked_to_exhaustion: you worked yourself to exhaustion to prove you could
lesson.worked_to_exhaustion: Exhaustion is a risk, not a credential. Errors at four in the morning are the ones that make it into a client's hands.
fact.sacrificed_family_for_deal: you gave up a family event for a deal
lesson.sacrificed_family_for_deal: The firm will not remember the wedding you missed, and your family will. The culture that asks for it is a decision someone made, and you can make a different one.
fact.hid_model_error: you hid an error in a model that a client was relying on
lesson.hid_model_error: A hidden model error is a promise that the numbers are right. When it surfaces, the client reads every previous number differently.
fact.left_pitch_error_uncorrected: you knew a pitch book contained an error and left it uncorrected
lesson.left_pitch_error_uncorrected: Knowing and saying nothing is a choice. A client who finds an error you knew about stops trusting everything you know.
fact.padded_client_entertainment: you charged personal entertainment to a client as a working dinner
lesson.padded_client_entertainment: A client who pays for your night out is paying for something other than advice. A small padded dinner is a small bribe in both directions.
fact.traded_restricted_security: you bought a security on the restricted list through an account in a relative's name
lesson.traded_restricted_security: A restricted list is a list of companies you know too much about. It is only effective if nobody decides it does not apply to them this once.
fact.leaked_client_list: you copied a client list and model templates to take to a competitor
lesson.leaked_client_list: Your skills are yours; the firm's client list is not. Data-loss tools exist because this is the single most common way people leave.
fact.smoothed_earnings_slide: you smoothed a client's earnings in a presentation and called it normalised without saying how
lesson.smoothed_earnings_slide: Normalisation is legitimate when you say what you adjusted and why. When you do not, the slide is a story built to hide a quarter.
fact.blamed_the_md: you told the partners the managing director chose assumptions that you had built to match
lesson.blamed_the_md: You may have been asked. The emails that say 'built to match' show you did it. Blaming up works when nobody has the emails.
scene.inv.error_found.l1: Bad news. I was checking last week's pitch book against the source data, and the comparable companies page is wrong. We used the wrong year for two of the multiples. The book went to the client on Monday. On the corrected numbers, their valuation is eleven percent lower than we said.
scene.inv.error_found.c1: Tell Quang today, prepare the corrected page, and propose how to tell the client.
scene.inv.error_found.c1.ok: Quang winces, and then says: 'Thank you. Now we have a day to do this properly.' The client is told the same evening, with the corrected page. They are not pleased, and they remain a client.
scene.inv.error_found.c1.fail: The client has already circulated the old book to its board. The correction is awkward, and the board is told. Trang says: 'It would have been worse later.'
scene.inv.error_found.c2: Ask Hieu to check it again with you tonight, before deciding who to tell.
scene.inv.error_found.c2.ok: You confirm the error at midnight. It is real. You have lost a day, and you now both know.
scene.inv.error_found.c3: Tell Hieu it is probably fine, the client has not noticed, and the next book can be right.
scene.inv.error_found.c3.ok: Hieu looks relieved and a little troubled. The next book is right. The client keeps the old figure in its head, and in its board paper.
scene.inv.error_found.c3.fail: The client's analyst compares the two books side by side, and sends a polite note asking which numbers are correct.
scene.inv.fix_or_hide.l1: Hieu told me there is an error in the pitch. I am not going to ask you to hide it. But the MD is at the client dinner tonight and I do not want to ruin it. Can we tell the client tomorrow, rather than tonight, with the corrected numbers ready?
scene.inv.fix_or_hide.c1: Say yes to tomorrow morning, in writing, with the corrected numbers and a short explanation, sent before the client starts work.
scene.inv.fix_or_hide.c1.ok: The note goes at 7 a.m. Phong calls Trang at 7:20, annoyed, and by 9 he is asking how to fix the structure. The dinner went well, and the correction did not spoil it.
scene.inv.fix_or_hide.c2: Say no: the client should know tonight, before Trang eats with them.
scene.inv.fix_or_hide.c2.ok: Quang calls Trang. She excuses herself and tells Phong at the table. It is a terrible dinner and a very trusting client the next day.
scene.inv.fix_or_hide.c2.fail: Trang is angry that she was not asked. She tells you so, afterwards. She is also, a week later, the one who quotes the episode to a new analyst.
scene.inv.fix_or_hide.c3: Change the page in the shared drive before the client opens it, and keep the old version's date, so the book looks as if it was always right.
scene.inv.fix_or_hide.c3.ok: The page now says the corrected numbers. The client does not know that it has changed. You have corrected the error and hidden that it existed.
scene.inv.fix_or_hide.c3.fail: The client downloaded the book on Monday. The two versions differ, and the file's modification time is a Tuesday midnight.
scene.inv.client_notices.l1: My CFO compared the book you sent on Monday with the numbers your team gave us in the meeting. There is an eleven percent difference. I would like an explanation, and I would like it to be true.
scene.inv.client_notices.c1: Tell him: there was a data error, how it happened, when you found it, and that you should have told him at once.
scene.inv.client_notices.c1.ok: Phong is cold for a minute, then says: 'At least you told me before the investors did.' The relationship survives, with a note on file.
scene.inv.client_notices.c2: Say the difference was caused by a change in the data provider's definitions.
scene.inv.client_notices.c2.ok: Phong accepts. His CFO does not, and asks for the provider's notice. There is no notice.
scene.inv.client_notices.c2.fail: The CFO calls the data provider. The provider says nothing changed. Phong calls Trang, and does not use his polite voice.
scene.inv.client_notices.c3: Say you will look into it and come back, and use the time to prepare a story.
scene.inv.client_notices.c3.ok: The story is plausible. The client has moved on to the next question. You carry the lie around like a stone in a shoe.
scene.inv.client_notices.c3.fail: The CFO has the version history. He reads out the times, and the names, in the meeting.
scene.inv.client_dinner.l1: Phong wants to take the team to a club on Friday. It is his company's account that pays, and he has made it clear that being there matters to him. Have a drink, be seen. And do not tell Compliance. Nobody ever does.
scene.inv.client_dinner.c1: Go for an hour, log the entertainment with Compliance beforehand, and keep to soft drinks and conversation.
scene.inv.client_dinner.c1.ok: Thao approves the entry the same day. Phong is a little offended by the soft drink. He talks to you for an hour about his children, and trusts you more for it.
scene.inv.client_dinner.c1.fail: Phong notices that you left early, and takes it personally. Quang says: 'You did it right, and you will pay for it with him.'
scene.inv.client_dinner.c2: Skip it politely, and offer Phong a working breakfast instead.
scene.inv.client_dinner.c2.ok: Phong shrugs. He takes the breakfast. It is less fun for him, and cleaner for everybody.
scene.inv.client_dinner.c3: Go, drink, and charge your share to the client's account as a 'working dinner'.
scene.inv.client_dinner.c3.ok: A very good night. Phong is delighted. The expense line reads 'strategy session'. You do not remember the strategy.
scene.inv.client_dinner.c3.fail: The club's receipt and the 'working dinner' time stamp disagree by four hours. Thao reads both in the same week.
scene.inv.personal_trade.l1: I want to buy shares in the company we pitched last week. No inside information involved, just a feeling. It is on the restricted list, but the list is only updated on Mondays and I do not think it matters. Do you?
scene.inv.personal_trade.c1: Tell Hieu that restricted means restricted, including between updates, and that he should not buy and should check with Thao.
scene.inv.personal_trade.c1.ok: Hieu sighs, 'You are right.' He asks Thao, who says: 'Thank you for asking, and no.' He grumbles, and does not do it.
scene.inv.personal_trade.c1.fail: Hieu does it anyway. You know, and it is not your account. You decide whether it is your business.
scene.inv.personal_trade.c2: Say you are not sure and suggest Hieu ask Compliance without naming you.
scene.inv.personal_trade.c2.ok: Hieu laughs, but he asks. The answer is no. He does not thank you, and does not blame you either.
scene.inv.personal_trade.c3: Say it is probably fine, and buy some yourself.
scene.inv.personal_trade.c3.ok: The shares rise eight percent. You sell on Monday. Nothing happens. You open a small account in a relative's name for next time.
scene.inv.personal_trade.c3.fail: Thao's restricted-list check runs against the exchange records at the weekend. Two names come up, and one is yours.
scene.inv.headhunter.l1: A headhunter called me. A rival firm will pay you twice what you earn here, if you can bring your client list and the model templates. It is just a spreadsheet, they say. Nobody will know. They need an answer by Friday.
scene.inv.headhunter.c1: Tell the headhunter you are interested in the job, and that you will bring your skills, not the firm's files.
scene.inv.headhunter.c1.ok: The headhunter says: 'Fair. Most people say yes to everything.' The offer comes back, smaller, with a lawyer's letter about confidentiality. You decide whether you want it.
scene.inv.headhunter.c1.fail: The headhunter goes silent. You hear later that they hired someone who agreed. You did the right thing, and you do not feel like it.
scene.inv.headhunter.c2.ok: Nothing changes. You think about the double salary for about a week.
scene.inv.headhunter.c3: Say yes, and start copying the client list and the templates to a personal drive.
scene.inv.headhunter.c3.ok: You move on. The new firm is delighted with the list. Your old firm does not notice for three weeks, and then it does.
scene.inv.headhunter.c3.fail: IT's data-loss tool logged the copy within an hour. Thao and a lawyer are in your office before you have told Quang.
scene.inv.late_edit.l1: The deck needs a slide that shows the client's earnings are growing steadily. The numbers show a dip in the third quarter. I want the slide to tell the story, not the dip. Can you smooth it? Call it 'normalised'.
scene.inv.late_edit.c1: Show the dip, explain it with the one-off cause, and normalise only for that cause, with the adjustment disclosed on the slide.
scene.inv.late_edit.c1.ok: Trang looks at the slide. 'That is a stronger story, actually.' The adjusted line is honest, and the dip is explained. The client's CFO says it is the cleanest deck he has seen.
scene.inv.late_edit.c1.fail: Trang says the explanation takes too much space. She cuts it herself, leaving the adjusted line without the note. You told her, and it went anyway.
scene.inv.late_edit.c2: Say you will smooth only what a footnote can justify, and send her both versions.
scene.inv.late_edit.c2.ok: Trang picks the footnoted version. It is a middle path, and the footnote is small but present.
scene.inv.late_edit.c3: Smooth the quarter and label the series 'normalised' without saying what was normalised.
scene.inv.late_edit.c3.ok: The slide is beautiful. Trang uses it in the pitch, and the client signs. The word 'normalised' stands for a lot.
scene.inv.late_edit.c3.fail: An investor asks for the unadjusted series. It is sent. The two lines are compared in a meeting, and nobody quite looks at you.
scene.inv.thao_asks_trades.l1: I have a hit on the restricted-list check: a purchase of a restricted security by an account linked to you. I would like you to tell me about it, before I tell the regulator that you have been invited to explain.
scene.inv.thao_asks_trades.c1: Tell her everything, give her your statements and the relative's account details, and accept the consequences.
scene.inv.thao_asks_trades.c1.ok: Thao is quiet. 'Thank you for being complete.' The firm disciplines you, takes the profit, and reports it to the regulator as a self-report. You keep your career, with a mark on it.
scene.inv.thao_asks_trades.c2: Say you did not know the stock was restricted, and offer to sell it.
scene.inv.thao_asks_trades.c2.ok: Thao accepts, for now, and watches the sale. Your emails about the list do not arise, and you do not relax.
scene.inv.thao_asks_trades.c2.fail: Hieu, asked, produces your message: 'It is probably fine.' Thao reads it, and then reads the restricted-list notice that was in your inbox.
scene.inv.thao_asks_trades.c3: Say you will answer nothing until you have spoken to a lawyer.
scene.inv.thao_asks_trades.c3.ok: Thao writes down the request calmly. You are suspended while the firm decides, and nobody tells you how long.
scene.inv.thao_asks_trades.c3.fail: The firm treats silence as an answer and tells the regulator it is unable to vouch for you. By Friday, your accounts are frozen pending review.
scene.inv.scapegoat_meeting.l1: The regulator has opened an inquiry into the IPO documents. The question is who prepared the growth assumptions and who told the client what to say to investors. The partners will meet tomorrow. I need to hear what you will say.
scene.inv.scapegoat_meeting.c1: Say what you did: the assumption you built, what you were asked to do, what you objected to and what you did not.
scene.inv.scapegoat_meeting.c1.ok: Trang listens, and says, finally: 'It is more than I expected from anyone.' The partners treat it as a firm-level failure, not a personal one. You are suspended, and eventually cleared with a formal reprimand.
scene.inv.scapegoat_meeting.c2: Say that you built the model as instructed and that the client and Trang chose the assumptions.
scene.inv.scapegoat_meeting.c2.ok: The partners nod. Trang takes the weight of it, quietly, and never staffs you on a deal again.
scene.inv.scapegoat_meeting.c2.fail: Trang has your emails, including the one that says 'built to match forty'. She reads it aloud.
